\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Finite Law}

\section{Overview}
The sharp weighted finite-noise estimate transfers to every centered measurable random variable with a finite law and the prescribed minimum atom mass.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp affine contraction for finite laws]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_law_sharp_forward}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_affine_norm_sq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_law_integral, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteLaw.finite_probability_atom_weights, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.HasAtomLowerBound.memLp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.IsHypercontractive, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_duality, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_sharp_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.radius_pos_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rvLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{5}
Let $q>2$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and let $X$ be a centered measurable real random variable on a probability space, supported almost surely on a finite set whose atoms each have mass at least $\lambda$. Then $H_{2,q,\rho_*(q,\lambda)}(X)$ holds. Here $\rho_*(q,\lambda)=\sqrt{\sinh(\ell/q)/\sinh(\ell/(q/(q-1)))}$ with $\ell=\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)$. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
\end{theorem}
